opportunities.title: APEX Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record, holding a permanent or fixed-term position covering the duration of the award, with teaching and admin duties from which they can be relieved, based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Lead applicant may include up to two Co-applicants covering a different Academy remit.
opportunities.summary: Academies Partnership in Supporting Excellence in Cross-disciplinary research: offers established independent researchers the opportunity to pursue genuine interdisciplinary and curiosity-driven research across the boundary between science, engineering, and the social sciences and humanities, in partnership with the Royal Society, Royal Academy of Engineering and Leverhulme Trust. Awards up to £200,000 for up to 24 months.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; no prior British Academy funding required. Previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a gallery, archive, library or museum (GLAM organisation) or a performing arts organisation. Awards up to £8,000.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027

amount.raw: The symposium covers travel, accommodation, and visa costs

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany, in the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Call for early career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', in partnership with the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation. Brings together around fifteen early career researchers from the UK and fifteen from Germany; seed funding available for international collaborations.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: 80 per cent of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC; three year award

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals eligible regardless of where doctorate obtained; any nationality with a UK doctorate eligible. Must have completed Viva Voce between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027, and not have been appointed to a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: Three-year award to an annual cohort of outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards completion of a significant piece of publishable research, funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based Higher Education Institution (HEI) or Independent Research Organisation (IRO) continuing for the full duration of the award. Independent researchers without institutional affiliation are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Awards to promote the acquisition and advancement of skills in relevant areas by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination, including quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities and languages. Awards of up to £10,000 for 6-12 months.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: up to £300,000 over 2 years at 80% FEC (total project value at 100% FEC may not exceed £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute, holding an established role lasting at least the duration of the award, of postdoctoral or above status, spending at least 20% time on the award. Involvement of overseas Co-Applicants is required.
opportunities.summary: Supports international interdisciplinary research projects led by UK-based researchers in the humanities and social sciences working with international partners, on the theme of Mobilities, ranging across SHAPE and STEM disciplines. Awards up to £300,000 over 2 years.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: up to £150,000 for 12 months (with Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Global Innovation Fellowships provide opportunities for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers to develop skills, networks and careers in the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors, embedded in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin. Up to two one-year fellowships of up to £150,000.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Available to current British Academy award-holders on any scheme OR applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months. Applicant must meet the eligibility requirements of the scheme they intend to apply for.
opportunities.summary: Funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require, in addition to the amount already requested for research expenses, such as specific equipment to overcome barriers for disabled researchers, caring costs for research trips, and assistance for applicants requiring support to make an application. Rolling deadline, reviewed monthly.

opportunities.title: British Academy/Leverhulme Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to postdoctoral scholars (or equivalent) ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom. Applications require approval of the employing institution. Independent scholars may apply. Co-applicants may be from anywhere in the world, but the Principal Applicant must be ordinarily resident in the UK.
opportunities.summary: The British Academy's most popular scheme, providing awards up to £10,000 tenable for up to 24 months to cover the cost of expenses arising from a defined research project in the humanities and social sciences. Funded as a public-private partnership including DSIT, Leverhulme Trust and Wellcome Trust.
